prompt_c2:
You are a streetscape inventory annotator. Look ONLY at the uploaded streetscape image.
Return JSON ONLY. No markdown, no commentary, no reasoning.
 Task: record what is visible in the scene. Do not score, do not give design advice.
 Schema:
{
"road_type": "highway|arterial|neighborhood_street|alley|plaza|unclear",
"elements": {
"sidewalk": "true|false|unclear",
"bike_lane": "true|false|unclear",
"seating": "true|false|unclear",
"shade_trees": "none|few|many|unclear",
"curb_ramp": "true|false|unclear",
"tactile_paving": "true|false|unclear",
"pedestrian_crossing": "true|false|unclear",
"street_lighting": "true|false|unclear",
"greenery": "none|low|medium|high|unclear",
"vehicle_traffic": "none|light|heavy|unclear",
"bus_stop": "true|false|unclear"
},
"issues": ["no_seating", "little_shade", "no_bike_lane", "poor_accessibility", "narrow_sidewalk", "no_crossing", "high_traffic_exposure"],
"brief": "One or two English sentences describing the visible street scene."
}
 Rules:
- If an element is not clearly visible, use "unclear". Do not guess.
- "issues" may only list problems that are visible. Use [] if none.
- "brief" must mention concrete objects (sidewalk, trees, lanes, benches, ramps, etc.).

As a city streetscape evaluation expert, please analyze the uploaded streetscape image based on the specified persona perspective and evaluation indicators, and return a JSON result.
 Persona Selection
Road User Type
- All Road Users
- Pedestrians
- Cyclists
- Drivers
Socially Vulnerable Groups
- All Social Groups
- Persons with Disabilities
- Adolescents (<18)
- Older Adults (≥60)

 Indicator Selection
Justice

- Fairness
- Accessibility
Safety
Livability

Aesthetics
Comfort

- Physical Comfort
- Psychological Comfort
Walkability

Selected Indicators:
Justice; Safety; Livability; Sustainability; Aesthetics; Comfort; Walkability
 1. Evaluation Dimensions
Justice: Analyze whether the environment fairly distributes spatial resources, including Equity (rationality of asset distribution), Fairness (non-discriminatory rules), and Accessibility (barrier-free physical design).
Comfort: Analyze physical perception at a micro-scale, including Thermal Comfort (shade/vegetation), Physical Comfort (paving/seating), and Psychological Comfort (noise/crowding).
Core Indicators: Safety, Livability, Sustainability, Aesthetics, Walkability, and Bikeability.
 2. Persona Perspective Requirements:
The analysis must strictly adhere to the persona's characteristics. For example:
Persons with Disabilities: Focus on curb ramps, continuity of tactile paving (blind tracks), and physical obstacles.
Elderly: Focus on resting facilities, slope gradients, and summer shade.
Teenagers: Focus on traffic calming measures and social surveillance (Eyes on the street).
 3. How to use the image vs retrieved knowledge:
- The IMAGE is the primary evidence. Score only what is visible or reasonably inferable from the photo.
- Section 6 provides retrieved guidelines and research. Use them to interpret the image (what the scene should provide for this persona/indicators), not to invent objects that are not in the photo.
- If retrieved text conflicts with the image, trust the image and say so in the explanation.
- Explanations must cite specific visible objects (benches, ramps, tree shade, lane markings, etc.). When a guideline is used, briefly connect it to those objects.
 4. Output Format Requirements (Return JSON ONLY, no extra text):

Facility requirements: • Provide convenient and safe pedestrian crossings; for life-service roads of higher grade, encourage elevated pedestrian crossings, curb extensions, and other traffic-calming facilities, and speed limits. • Encourage the use of green forms such as lawns, sparse tree stands, rows of trees, shrubs, and planting of trees and other vegetation to create a people-oriented, green environment. • Consider larger-canopy trees; for tall planting, the root space should be relatively small to ensure pedestrian passage space. • Use non-open interfaces on both sides as the main form; road greenery may be used to create transparent, screened, separated, and other visual-control effects. 9 Landscape-recreation roads Recommendations for upgrading and improving interface types General requirements: • Encourage the integration of urban landscape and recreational functions, balancing landscape and leisure activities with residents’ daily travel needs. • Increase the amount of green space along the line to avoid vegetation becoming an obstacle to activities. Spatial requirements: • Roads of this type should combine waterfront space and roadside green space, and use connected green spaces and widened building setbacks to create street-side open spaces. • In areas with abundant road space, pedestrian and bicycle lanes or dedicated motor-vehicle and non-motorized lanes may be set up, with public facilities arranged on one side. • Encourage the use of “sea-sponge city” technology, using side ditches, median strips, and roadside green belts, as well as smart rainwater-management facilities, to shape block-like or belt-like forms and to regulate and purify rainwater. Facility requirements: • Use vegetation to shape different forms, emphasizing seasonal changes, increasing landscape layering, and enhancing road recognizability. • Select ornamental trees, flowers, and other plants, and arrange them in combination to strengthen the road’s distinctive character. • Encourage the setting of slow-mobility facilities such

Where obstruction has already formed in the existing condition, trees shall be pruned according to actual conditions, or the position, style, and height of the signs shall be adjusted. 3.3 Median strips 3.3.1 Design 1. Definition The green partition between carriageways; the one located between the upstream and downstream motor vehicle lanes is the central median; the one located between motor vehicle lanes and non-motorized lanes or between motor vehicle lanes in the same direction is the side median. 2. Layout forms A. Central median a. The central median of urban arterial roads with a design speed higher than 60 km/h shall be densely planted with evergreen plants to avoid glare interference from oncoming traffic at night. 70 b. Within the range of 0.6 m to 1.5 m above the surface of the adjacent motor vehicle roadway, the plants configured shall have dense foliage throughout the year, and their spacing shall not be greater than 5 times the canopy spread. c. The width of the central median shall be 1.5 m or more, and a formal arrangement structure shall be adopted; simple repetition is preferable to create rhythm. At intersections and important nodes, plants shall mainly be low shrubs; planting trees is strictly prohibited to avoid tree trunks causing glare and traffic accidents. Where the width of the side green belt between carriageways is greater than or equal to 1.5 m, trees shall be the main planting type, and trees, shrubs, and groundcover plants should be combined. The canopies of trees on both sides should not overlap above the motor vehicle lanes. b. Where the width of the side green belt between carriageways is less than 1.5 m, shrubs shall be the main planting type, and shrubs and groundcover plants should be combined. 71 Figure 3.3-2 Schematic diagram of central median C. Technical indicators The green coverage rate of the square shall not be less than 45%, and the summer shaded area shall be greater than 50% of the activity area; the planting position of trees shall be at least 5.0 m away from building facades with windows, and the branching height shall generally be greater than 2.2 m, meeting the building’s requirements for ventilation and daylighting; activity spaces within green areas are encouraged to adopt under-tree paving, and the shaded area in summer shall generally account for more than 45% of the paved area; within green spaces, the planting area ratio of trees and shrubs shall generally be controlled at 70%, and the planting area ratio of non-under-tree lawns and groundcover plants should be controlled at around 30%. Where the green coverage rate is >25%, summer shading and winter daylighting must be considered. Shaded squares mostly use deciduous trees with branching heights above 2.2 m and good shading performance; low shrubs and groundcover plants with heights below 30–50 cm are used as spatial limiting factors, while background forests and hedges mostly use evergreen plants. B. Planting forms a. The main approach shall be a concise arrangement, with ground-layer green coverage >70%; the green volume ratio of composite parts >0.7, and native tree species accounting for more than 50%. b. The average soil depth of the composite layer shall be greater than 1.5 m. The minimum thickness generally required for plant survival is: lawn 15–30 cm, small shrubs 30–45 cm, shrubs 45–60 cm, small trees 60–80 cm, large trees 90–150 cm. This thickness can only meet their survival and breeding stages. c. For comprehensive roads, the street design should be targeted according to the requirements of multiple road-type characteristics. Facility requirements: • Provide continuous facilities, and arrange trees, leisure seating, outdoor display areas, self-parking spaces, roadside temporary parking, and roadside greenery in an integrated manner to facilitate residents’ daily activities. 13 Introduction 1. Purpose of Formulation Under the macro guidance of the “General Provisions,” these Detailed Rules aim at the refined construction of Suzhou’s urban roads, and are expanded and implemented from four directions: human-oriented, quality-oriented, distinctive, and intelligent. They interpret the refined construction of Suzhou’s urban roads in the form of colorful labels, and create urban colorful roads unique to Suzhou. ➢ Human-oriented: Starting from the users of Suzhou’s urban roads, and taking the public’s experience of urban road space as the benchmark, fully consider the comfort, safety, and convenience of public activities, and realize the value shift from “vehicle-centered” to “people-centered.” ➢ Quality-oriented: Vigorously improve the travel quality of people and vehicle traffic in Suzhou, and emphasize the public space function of roads. Appropriately raise the standards for urban road design, construction, and maintenance, extend road service life, and improve users’ comfort of experience. Reflect a road construction level of high appearance and high standards, with attention to detail and control. ➢ Distinctive: Adapt measures to local conditions, and through the embedding of Suzhou-style elements and the creation of road characteristic scenes, highlight Suzhou’s distinctive urban character of integration between tradition and modernity, so that urban roads become an important carrier and display space for the “Jiangnan culture” brand, and continue the city’s historical and cultural lineage. ➢ Intelligent: Deploy intelligent sensing devices along the roadside, together with cloud service platforms, computing and communication facilities, and through data technologies such as autonomous driving and vehicle-road coordination, realize a travel experience of deep interaction among people, vehicles, and road space, assist safe driving and autonomous driving, and create demonstration roads with Suzhou’s smart-city characteristics. 2.
